metadata.title: Claude, Jira API.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether moving a Jira ticket to Done is a direct status write or something else, using the jira-api skill's own documented facts as the concrete case. Lands the carry-out that every write turns on two habits — a transition ID instead of a status you set, and a JSON tree instead of a string you type.

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('set' -> 'transition') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Ask Claude to move a ticket to Done, and it can't just write that value — Jira has no direct status field to set. It first lists the issue's available transitions, matches the one named Done, and posts that transition's ID. And that ID isn't universal: the same-looking transition on a different ticket, in a different workflow, often carries a different ID.

shot.new_visual_element: A direct status-write guess struck through; the actual path opened — list transitions, match by name, post by ID — with the same ID failing on a second ticket

production_viz.label: No status field — a transition, looked up first
production_viz.mechanic: A guessed write, 'status: Done', fades in, then gets struck through in terracotta. Beside it, the real path opens as three chips: list transitions, match 'Done' by name, post ID. A second ticket appears below with the same ID pasted in — it lands on a card marked with an X, a different ID card lighting up in its place.

beats.narration_text: Two families split the work: Platform REST v3 handles issues, projects, and search — the default — while Agile REST v1 only covers boards and sprints, concepts the core issue model doesn't have. Say Claude searches PROJ for every open bug assigned to you: that search has to be bounded — at least one filter clause, or it's rejected — and it comes back a page at a time, a token pointing to the next page instead of a total count. Comment on the top result, and that comment can't be a plain string: it has to be a JSON tree — a doc, versioned, built from typed content blocks — or Jira sends back a 400.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — two API families, then the bounded-search-plus-comment request traced through nextPageToken pagination and ADF

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — bounded search, paged by token, commented in ADF
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Two labelled tracks: Platform REST v3 (issues, projects, search) marked DEFAULT; Agile REST v1 (boards, sprints) marked ONLY WHEN NEEDED. Below, a request card — 'every open bug in PROJ, assigned to me' — sends a bounded JQL filter, a token chip passes to 'next page' instead of a total counter, then a comment card opens into a JSON tree: type doc, content array. THIS EXACT REQUEST RETURNS AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Get it right, and the loop stops the moment the token disappears — no total needed — and the comment posts clean as a typed JSON tree, not a sentence. Get it wrong, and it fails quietly two different ways: a loop written to expect a total from search never gets one, and can spin forever waiting; a comment sent as a plain string comes back a 400, but the error never mentions ADF, so it just looks broken. One more habit worth carrying: assignees and watchers take an account ID, never an email — Jira stopped accepting email lookups years ago.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same request completing when the token runs out and the ADF comment posts clean, then the same request silently spinning or 400ing when a habit is skipped, then accountId flagged

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — complete, then quietly wrong, then one more habit
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 REQUEST RETURNS, identical. Left: pages stack until the token chip goes empty, marked 'done — no total needed'; the comment card posts as a clean JSON tree. Right: a loop card waits on a total that never arrives, spinning; a plain-string comment card returns '400' with no mention of ADF, both marked 'looks broken' in terracotta. A small card breaks off to the side: 'accountId, not email' with an email icon struck through.

beats.narration_text: Every Jira write Claude makes turns on two habits — a transition ID instead of a status you set, and a JSON tree instead of a string you type — get those right, and the three pagination schemes are the only thing left to watch for.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Find all open bugs in PROJ assigned to me, then move the highest-priority one to In Progress and add a comment explaining why. Watch three things: does it list the issue's transitions and post by ID instead of trying to set status directly, does it send the comment as a JSON tree instead of a plain string, and does it keep paging through search results by token instead of stopping when it doesn't see a total. Liam, in for Bear.
